title: heuristic-handoff-patterns-gpu-reset-sleuth-2028-04-12
content:
Context:
This is a working note intended to capture an on-call -> daytime handoff pattern we tried during the recent cluster instability window. The focus is on building small, actionable heuristics the night team can leave for daytime engineers to prioritize root-cause experiments instead of a long freeform wall of logs.

Summary of incident pattern observed (Mar-Apr 2028):
- Symptom cluster: intermittent node resets with noisy prelude: sudden KV-cache invalidations, 2–5s of high PCIe link retries, then driver OOM or wedge followed by node-level reset (soft or hard depending on firmware).
- Telemetry signals correlated: elevated correctable ECC count (soft drift), asymmetric NVLink training retries (one side flap), and a rising "entropy_score" metric computed in the collector (see below).
- Impact: ~1.2% of inference capacity affected during peak windows; automated retries masked some customer errors but increased tail latency.

What we tried that worked (heuristic-level):
1) Entropy scoring: we computed a 0-1 score combining (normalized correctable ECC rate, NVLink retrain count, driver warning burst rate over 10m). When score > 0.6 on a node, mark node as "high-entropy" and increase sampling granularity (capture 60s full PMU + kernel messages). This reliably surfaced early NVLink negotiation failures.
2) Fast quarantine policy: To avoid noisy resets cascading, the oncall procedure quarantines node for 10 minutes when entropy_score > 0.8 AND eviction count > 3 in 5m. Quarantine = Cordon + disable autoscaler placement + disable scheduled workload restarts.
3) Watchdog soft-tune: lowered kernel watchdog timeout to 90s for suspected drivers (experimental) reduced hard resets; instead we got a clean driver unload path allowing syslog collection. We roll this out only in lab; truthing needed on prod after further bake.

On-call handoff template (short, copyable):
- Incident ID: (auto insert)
- First detection time: (UTC)
- Node(s): [hostnames list]
- Current entropy_score: (value)
- Actions taken (night): quarantine? yes/no; captures collected? (path)
- Immediate priority for day: (choose one) 1) reproduce NVLink negotiator with stress harness 2) correlate PMIC/PSU telemetry 3) schedule firmware A/B rollback trial
- Tentative hypothesis (1 line): e.g. "NVLink asymmetric handshake + soft ECC accumulation causing driver resource leak -> eviction -> reset"

Example short log snippet captured during a pre-reset window:
[2028-04-09T02:14:17Z] nvlink: train_retry_count=12 sideB_lane3
[2028-04-09T02:14:20Z] gpu: correctable_ecc_inc=27 total=143 window=600s
[2028-04-09T02:14:23Z] driver: ctx_alloc_warning: pid=4253 ctx=0x7f3e.. count=37
[2028-04-09T02:14:28Z] systemd: watchdog-kernel: hung task detected -> unloading driver
[2028-04-09T02:15:10Z] node-reset: reason=watchdog-driver-unload type=soft

Useful commands / quick captures (oncall frequently runs these and leaves results in the incident folder):
- collect-kvcache-snapshot /var/logs/kvcache-snap-$NODE-$(date +%s).tgz
- telemetry-sample --window=60s --metrics="nvlink_retrain,correctable_ecc,driver_warnings" --out=/tmp/ent-sample.json
- sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service --since "10 minutes ago" > /tmp/driver_events.log
- sudo ethtool -S pcie0 | grep retrain_count (our agent maps PCIe w/ NVLink lanes)

Fingerprinting approach (avoid chasing raw stack dumps):
- Create 3 fingerprint buckets: 
  A) nvlink-handshake -> patterns of retrain_count spikes + lane-specific errors
  B) ecc-drift -> sustained correctable increases without lane spikes
  C) driver-leak -> rapid ctx_alloc_warning bursts followed by OOM
- Tag incident with fingerprint early. Fingerprints help daytime teams pick targeted experiments instead of replaying the full capture.

Open hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent NVLink lane training failure caused by timing/regression in new retimer firmware (probability: medium-high).
2) PMIC transient undervolt events during high density bursts amplify ECC rates on some ASICs (probability: medium).
3) Driver change 2028-02 introduced a leak under specific workload alignment (probability: medium-low).

Planned daytime experiments (pick 1 per node):
- Lab repro: replay 75% real traffic from production using nvlink-stress harness with lane-level fault injection (JIRA: SRE-2143).
- Firmware trial: roll retimer firmware v2.1 -> v2.0 on small pool and observe entropy_score over 72h (change controlled by infra; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/firmware/PR-57).
- Telemetry densification: enable 1s sampling for nvlink and ECC counters on 4 suspect nodes for 24h.

Known limitations and risks of current heuristics:
- Entropy score thresholds are empirical; false positives during heavy multi-tenant bursts. We should add a workload-normalized baseline.
- Quarantine reduces capacity and may increase load on remaining nodes; need automated reroute to spare pool when quarantining more than 3 nodes in a rack.
- Watchdog soft-tune in lab avoided hard resets but may hide slow resource leaks that surface later.

Handoff checklist for morning follow-up (actionable):
- Confirm all quarantined nodes have full captures in /incidents/SRE-2143/captures (attach short summary).
- For each fingerprint=A: schedule lane-level repro in lab. Assign: Marcus Li.
- For fingerprint=B: request PSU/PMIC telemetry export from hardware team (ticket HW-45).
- For fingerprint=C: run heap/alloc tracing on driver in ephemeral env. Assign: Sophie Martinez.
- Post short note in #sre-ops summarizing current capacity loss and ETA for experiments.

Quick decision matrix (for oncall):
- If entropy_score > 0.9 and node reset rate > 3 in 30m -> immediate node quarantine + page SRE lead.
- If entropy_score between 0.6 and 0.9 and single reset -> capture + monitor for 60m, do not quarantine unless repeat.

Unresolved questions to prioritize in follow-up:
- Can we get lane-level physical layer logs from vendor? (RFP open, contact hw-vendor-eng)
- Is there a firmware release that coincided with an increase in retrain_count across rack X? (compare firmware manifests)
- Can we correlate cooling/power transient events with ECC bursts (cross-reference datacenter BMS logs)?

Next steps (short bullets with owners):
- Marcus Li: build a small repro harness that injects lane flaps and measures entropy_score change (ETA 5d).
- Sophie Martinez: prepare driver heap trace recipe and run against two suspect nodes in lab (ETA 3d).
- Evan Brooks: coordinate firmware rollback trial planning with infra (create runbook checklist and rollback play).

Appendix: short notes to help daytime sanity checks:
- entropy_score calculation: normalized(correctable_ecc_rate, nvlink_retrain_rate, driver_warning_rate) weighted [0.5, 0.3, 0.2] with rolling 10m smoothing.
- Capture retention: keep full captures 14 days, compressed summaries indefinitely.
- Incident folder convention: /incidents/YYYY-MM/ID/ with plaintext metadata 'handoff.txt' containing the one-line hypothesis.

Comments and freeform scratch (notes-to-self style):
- "Hand-off must be a short checklist. Day teams are drowning in captures otherwise."
- "Consider integrating entropy score into alerting but add a workload baseline to avoid fat-finger quarantines."
- "We should prototype a small UI tile in Console showing 'entropy hotspots' by rack — will help SOC & infra."

Jira quick links: SRE-2143 (main incident), HW-45 (PMIC telemetry request), SW-312 (telemetry agent PR).

End of working note.
